- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward modestly.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen peak forecasts.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price moving back toward 65–68 range), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% below model, apply a downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast).
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often overfits recent noise; use 10–15 day smoothing or ignore short-term sentiment spikes.
